chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A boy was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while people were making supplication for him, and he had 'qanaz' (a type of hair growth or marking). He refused to make supplication for him, so he ordered the shaving of his head, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the shaving of the hair of the belly.

key_terms.قَنَازِعُ: Plural of qanaz, referring to a specific type of hair growth or marking on the body, often discussed in the context of ritual shaving.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do when presented with a boy who had qanaz?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) declines a specific supplication for a boy marked by 'qanaz' (often interpreted as a tuft of hair or a physical sign), instead commanding the shaving of the head and belly hair. This incident is cited in the chapter on *Aqiqah* to establish the ritual purification and blessing of the newborn, linking physical grooming with spiritual intercession in early Shia jurisprudence.
